executive_summary.conclusion: Arngren is publicly crawlable and exposes a broad Norwegian product inventory, contact details and prices, but the sampled experience is difficult to interpret as a current, task-oriented catalogue. Product pages provide useful specifications and caveats, while legacy layout, mixed encoding, mixed languages and inconsistent purchase handoffs leave important buyer decisions unresolved or hard to verify.

not_checked: Rendered browser inspection timed out in the delegated audit surface; responsive layout, keyboard/focus behavior and interactive state were not checked.
No actual assistant answer/citation runs were recorded; visibility remains not_measured.
Search observations were bounded and do not establish ranking, citation probability or absence of third-party coverage.
Evidence sample was five first-party HTML pages: homepage, el-varer.html, moller.html, alkotester.html and the HTTP homepage duplicate.

findings.title: Homepage inventory is not organized around buyer tasks

evidence.observation: The homepage presents a very large mixed list of unrelated products and categories (vehicles, toys, electronics, robots and hobby items) with many image-only links; it also says products may be discontinued or have changed price. This makes a neutral question such as which electric vehicle fits a buyer's age/use case hard to resolve from the entry page.

suggested_action.summary: Create maintained category landing pages with audience, use case, current availability, specifications, price status and a clear next step.
suggested_action.mechanism: Task-oriented pages give crawlers and visitors a stable, quotable answer path instead of requiring interpretation of a legacy visual inventory.
suggested_action.verification: For electric vehicle, RC/hobby and electronics tasks, each landing page exposes a text title, audience/use case, current price or request-quote state, key constraints and a contact/order route without returning to the homepage.

findings.title: Purchase and availability instructions are inconsistent or deferred to contact

evidence.observation: The homepage warns that products may be gone or prices may have increased, while sampled product content mixes prices with instructions such as asking for freight price and contacting the seller. The alcohol-tester page provides a price and warranty but no visible order handoff in the inspected text; the Moller page links to an external order destination for a historical product.

suggested_action.summary: Standardize each product page's current-status and purchase handoff block.
suggested_action.mechanism: A consistent availability, delivery/collection, payment and contact block prevents users from inferring whether a displayed price is actionable.
suggested_action.verification: Every sampled product page states in text whether it is available, how to request shipping or buy, and where the next public step leads; stale products are explicitly archived or labelled historical.

suggested_action.summary: Repair UTF-8 rendering and add explicit current/reviewed dates plus language-consistent factual copy.
suggested_action.mechanism: Correctly rendered terms and dated status labels improve extraction of names, constraints, safety notes and current-vs-historical claims.
suggested_action.verification: Re-fetch the five sampled URLs and confirm Norwegian characters render correctly, historical claims are labelled, and safety/operating qualifiers remain adjacent to their products.

proactive_opportunities.title: Build a current electric-vehicle comparison hub
proactive_opportunities.rationale: The site repeatedly exposes electric cars, ATVs, scooters and bikes with age, speed, range and price attributes, but those facts are scattered across the inventory.
proactive_opportunities.mechanism: A maintained comparison page can connect audience, legal/use constraints, range, charging and price to concrete product pages.
proactive_opportunities.verification: A visitor can compare at least three current models and reach a verified contact or order route from each row.

readiness.detail: robots.txt is present with a sitemap hint and no parsed disallow groups; sampled pages returned HTTP 200. This describes policy, not actual provider access.
Static HTML exposes titles, product text, prices, contacts, constraints and links across five pages; some evidence has legacy encoding and image-heavy presentation.
Offer, product constraints and contact facts are answerable for sampled pages, but current availability/order status is partial or ambiguous for several routes.

Bounded retrieval found independent directory and marketplace references that corroborate Arngren's Oslo identity and product categories; third-party listings also show dates and prices that should not be treated as current first-party inventory.
Static link paths were inspected, but rendered browser interaction timed out in this delegated surface; no form was submitted and no purchase/authentication step was attempted.
